prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the Green Party Manifesto 2024 (≤500 words)

Context and vision
- Address the cost-of-living and climate emergencies together: deliver a fairer society with rapid decarbonisation, better public services and community well-being grounded in science and justice.

Health and social care
- NHS: keep fully public; reduce waiting lists; rapid GP access; universal NHS dentistry; invest £8bn extra in year one, rising to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years; fair pay and staffing.
- Primary care/public health: more funding, diagnostics in communities, restore public health budgets, national commission to reform drug laws.
- Mental health: parity with physical health; therapies within 28 days; counsellor in every school.
- Social care: free personal care; £20bn/year; rebuild workforce with pay, training and fair visas; better support for disabled people and carers.

Homes and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes annually; end Right to Buy; rent controls; end no-fault evictions.
- Retrofit and standards: £29bn over five years to insulate homes to EPC B; grants for heat pumps (£9bn/5 years); cool homes adaptation (£7bn/5 years); Passivhaus-standard new builds; solar and low-carbon heat mandated; area-based, council-led delivery; bring empty homes into use.

Energy and climate
- No new oil and gas; cancel recent licences; carbon tax scaling to £500/t within 10 years.
- Renewables: wind ~70% of electricity by 2030; targets by 2035 of 80GW offshore, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar; end onshore wind barriers; expand grid, storage, interconnectors; community ownership minimums.
- Nuclear: stop new build; phase out existing stations.

Economy, work and welfare
- Green economic transformation: average £40bn/year investment (energy, retrofit, rail, public transport, active travel, water/sewage); bring rail, water and Big 5 retail energy companies into public ownership.
- Finance: align Bank of England mandate with climate; fossil divestment timelines; regional mutual banks; late payment enforcement.
- Workers’ rights: repeal anti-union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15 minimum wage; 10:1 pay ratio cap; day-one rights; gig workers classed as workers.
- Social security: +£40/week to Universal Credit and legacy benefits; scrap two-child cap and sanctions; end five-week wait; uplift disability benefits 5%; protect pensions; UBI as long-term goal.

Tax and public finances
- Wealth tax: 1% on assets >£10m; 2% >£1bn.
- Align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; fairer inheritance and property taxes; steps toward Land Value Tax.
- Carbon tax as above; windfall taxes; targeted VAT changes; borrow to invest.

Nature, animals and food
- Rights of Nature Act; 30% of land and sea protected by 2030; public ownership of water; stronger DEFRA, EA and Natural England; Right to Roam.
- Ban blood sports; end factory farming practices; protect marine areas; Commission on Animal Protection.
- Food: universal free school meals; reduce ultra-processed food harms; triple farm support to shift to nature-friendly, mixed farming and horticulture; fair supply chains.

Education
- Free, inclusive education; end tuition fees and restore grants; £8bn extra for schools plus £2.5bn/year for safe buildings; £5bn for SEND; end high-stakes testing and Ofsted; expand Sure Start and childcare; boost FE/skills.

Transport
- Public transport first: £10bn/year subsidies by end of parliament; £19bn over five years for upgrades; rail in public ownership; free buses for under-18s; £2.5bn/year for active travel; oppose new roads; road pricing; end new petrol/diesel sales by 2027, phase-out use by 2035; EV scrappage scheme; aviation frequent-flyer levy, no airport expansion, kerosene taxed, ban short domestic flights (<3h by rail).

Democracy, rights and migration
- Proportional representation; replace Lords; votes at 16; repeal voter ID and protest curbs; defend HRA/ECHR; trans self-ID.
- Migration: end hostile environment and NRPF; safe routes; right to work for asylum seekers; simplify and humanise visas; new Department of Migration.

Justice and drugs
- Community policing, restorative justice; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; tackle VAWG; decriminalise personal drug possession; invest £11bn in MoJ to cut backlogs and restore legal aid.

Foreign policy
- Ceasefire in Gaza; recognise Palestine; end UK arms exports to Israel; support Ukraine; increase aid to 1% of GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; pathway to rejoin EU (Customs Union, free movement, Erasmus); sign TPNW and cancel Trident; reform NATO with No First Use.
